## Overview

*This page is auto-generated from city documents. Last source: City Charter 2024 (2026-06-03)*

## Key Facts

- City Charter adopted by voters on November 5, 2024, replacing previous version from 2015 [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- City government consists of Mayor and seven Council members elected at-large for three-year terms [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- Council members occupy numbered positions (Place One through Place Seven) [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- Qualification requirements: must be 18 years old, registered voter, and resident for 12 consecutive months before filing deadline [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- City Manager serves as chief administrative officer, appointed by and responsible to City Council [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- Mayor serves as official head and Council chairman but votes only in case of tie [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- Mayor Pro-Tem appointed by City Council to serve during Mayor's absence [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- Fiscal year begins October 1 and ends September 30 [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]

### From City Charter 2024 (2026-06-03)

*From: City Charter 2024 (2026-06-03)*

- The City of Schertz operates under a Mayor-Council form of government with an appointed City Manager who serves at the will and pleasure of City Council [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- City Council consists of a Mayor and seven Council members, all elected at-large for three-year terms [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- Council members must be at least 18 years old, registered voters, and residents of Schertz for at least 12 consecutive months prior to filing deadline [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- The Mayor votes only in the event of a tie; four Council members (excluding the Mayor) constitute a quorum [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- The fiscal year begins on the first day of October and ends on the last day of the following September [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- Regular city elections are held annually on the uniform election date in November [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- Initiative, referendum, and recall petitions require signatures equal to at least 15% of registered voters from the last general city election [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- Charter amendments may be proposed by charter commission, City Council ordinance with majority vote, or petition signed by at least 5% of qualified voters [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- A Charter Review Commission must be appointed at least every five years to review city government operations [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]
- The City Manager is the chief administrative officer responsible for administration of all city affairs, appointing and removing employees, and preparing the annual budget [SOURCE: City Charter 2024]

### From TMRS-2019 Rate Letter (2023-03-17)

*From: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter (2023-03-17)*

- City of Schertz TMRS contribution rate for 2019 set at 16.16% (16.04% retirement + 0.12% Supplemental Death Benefit) [SOURCE: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter]
- City pension plan funded ratio improved from 73.2% (2016) to 74.7% (2017) [SOURCE: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter]
- TMRS plan has 322 active members, 98 retirees/beneficiaries, and 166 inactive members as of December 31, 2017 [SOURCE: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter]
- Unfunded pension liability of $16.7 million represents 94.9% of annual payroll [SOURCE: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter]
- Employee deposit rate is 7% with a 2-to-1 city matching ratio [SOURCE: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter]
- Retirement eligibility is age 60 with 5 years of service or 20 years of service at any age [SOURCE: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter]
- Plan provides 70% of CPI repeating annuity increases to retirees [SOURCE: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter]
- BAF crediting rate for 2017 was 13.05%, significantly higher than the 6.73% in 2016 [SOURCE: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter]
- Return on Actuarial Value of Assets was 6.96% in 2017, slightly above assumed 6.75% [SOURCE: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter]
- Vesting requires 5 years of service [SOURCE: TMRS-2019 Rate Letter]

*From: TMRS-2020 Rate Letter (2023-03-17)*

- City of Schertz TMRS contribution rate for 2020 set at 15.92% (15.80% retirement + 0.12% supplemental death benefit) [SOURCE: TMRS-2020 Rate Letter]
- Pension funded ratio improved from 74.7% in 2017 to 76.3% in 2018 [SOURCE: TMRS-2020 Rate Letter]

- Employee deposit rate is 7% with 2-to-1 city matching ratio [SOURCE: TMRS-2020 Rate Letter]

### From TMRS-2023 Rate Letter (2023-03-17)

*From: TMRS-2023 Rate Letter (2023-03-17)*

- TMRS uses a 10-year smoothing method for asset valuations to reduce contribution rate volatility [SOURCE: TMRS-2023 Rate Letter]

### From Employee Compensation Report FY23 FINAL (2024-12-13)

*From: Employee Compensation Report FY23 FINAL (2024-12-13)*

- FY2023 covered the period from October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023 [SOURCE: Employee Compensation Report FY23 FINAL]
- The city employs 437 staff members across all departments and categories [SOURCE: Employee Compensation Report FY23 FINAL]
- Employee categories include Civilian and Uniform positions [SOURCE: Employee Compensation Report FY23 FINAL]
- Total compensation includes regular earnings, overtime, additional earnings (certification pay, education pay, longevity, allowances, on-call pay, wellness, holiday pay), deployment earnings, benefits (FICA/Medicare, TMRS pension, healthcare premiums), and leave payouts [SOURCE: Employee Compensation Report FY23 FINAL]

- Additional benefits averaged approximately 30-40% of total earnings for most employees [SOURCE: Employee Compensation Report FY23 FINAL]

### From 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy (2025-11-14)

*From: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy (2025-11-14)*

- The City Manager and Finance Director serve as Investment Officers for the City of Schertz [SOURCE: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy]
- Investment Officers must receive 10 hours of training within first 12 months of assuming duties and 8 hours every 2 years thereafter [SOURCE: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy]
- The Investment Advisory Committee consists of City Manager (Chair), Deputy City Manager, Assistant City Manager, Executive Director of Economic Development, Finance Director, Assistant Finance Director, Budget/Financial Analyst, and up to three City Council representatives [SOURCE: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy]
- The Investment Advisory Committee meets at least semiannually to review investment portfolio [SOURCE: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy]
- Investment policy must be reviewed annually by City Council in compliance with Texas Public Funds Investment Act [SOURCE: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy]
- All investment transactions must use delivery vs. payment method through Federal Reserve System (except investment pool funds and mutual funds) [SOURCE: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy]
- Primary investment objectives are safety of principal, liquidity, diversification, yield, and public trust [SOURCE: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy]
- Maximum maturity of any security is five years with maximum dollar weighted average maturity of one year or less [SOURCE: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy]
- The City maintains one commingled portfolio incorporating all fund types [SOURCE: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy]
- Monthly investment reports must be provided to City Council [SOURCE: 24-R-09 Investment Policy and Strategy]

### From 50-876 (2025-08-20)

*From: 50-876 (2025-08-20)*

- The proposed FY2025 tax rate is $0.5350 per $100 valuation, representing a 5.6% increase from the FY2024 rate of $0.4900 [SOURCE: 50-876]
- The no-new-revenue tax rate for FY2025 is $0.5064 per $100, which would generate the same revenue as 2024 from the same properties [SOURCE: 50-876]
- The proposed rate equals the voter-approval tax rate, meaning no election is required for adoption [SOURCE: 50-876]
- Average homestead taxable values decreased 2.9% from $343,118 (2024) to $331,835 (2025) [SOURCE: 50-876]
- Despite declining property values, the average homestead tax bill would increase by $100 (6.0%) from $1,675.32 to $1,775.32 [SOURCE: 50-876]
- Total property tax levy would increase by $2,927,570 (10.5%) from $27.75 million to $30.68 million [SOURCE: 50-876]
- Public hearing on the proposed tax rate is scheduled for September 2, 2025 at 6 PM at City Council Chambers [SOURCE: 50-876]
- The 86th Texas Legislature modified voter-approval tax rate calculations to limit property tax growth in Texas [SOURCE: 50-876]
- Tax assessor contact: (830) 379-2315 or daryl.john@co.guadalupe.tx.us [SOURCE: 50-876]
- City Council voted 6-1 in favor of the proposed tax rate increase, with Councilmember Davis as the sole dissenting vote [SOURCE: 50-876]

### From 50-876 (3) (2025-08-08)

*From: 50-876 (3) (2025-08-08)*

- Form 50-876 is required under Texas Tax Code §§26.06(b-2) for tax rate notices [SOURCE: 50-876 (3)]
- The no-new-revenue tax rate maintains the same property tax revenue from the same properties year-over-year [SOURCE: 50-876 (3)]
- The voter-approval tax rate is the highest rate that can be adopted without holding an election [SOURCE: 50-876 (3)]
- The 86th Texas Legislature modified voter-approval tax rate calculations to limit property tax growth [SOURCE: 50-876 (3)]
- Property tax formula: (tax rate) x (taxable value) / 100 [SOURCE: 50-876 (3)]
- Counties may adjust no-new-revenue rates for state criminal justice mandates, indigent health care, indigent defense, and eligible county hospital expenditures [SOURCE: 50-876 (3)]
- Taxpayers can visit Texas.gov/PropertyTaxes to access local property tax databases [SOURCE: 50-876 (3)]
